newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt ally says not pessimistic over EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt ally says not pessimistic over EMU.

text.p: The leader of a party allied to the government said on Wednesday he was not pessimistic about Italy's chances of being a founder EMU member despite European Commission forecasts that Rome would miss a key criterion in 1997 and 1998.
"It's worrying in the sense that we need a last push, but I am not pessimistic," Franco Marini, leader of the centrist Popular Party, told reporters.
Earlier, the Commission said it expected Italy's budget deficit would be 3.2 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 and 3.9 percent in 1998.
Under the terms of the Maastricht Treaty, founder members of European economic and monetary union (EMU) are required to have a GDP/deficit ratio of three percent.

Marini said Italy's deficit/GDP ratio was close to seven percent in 1996 and added that Prime Minister Romano Prodi had introduced budget measures to lower the deficit this year which had to be fully implemented.
"For this reason, I'm not at all pessimistic," Marini said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
